summary: Discovery with Silverpike Labs focused on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for PLG onramp, tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC), and initial security requirements. Agreed to a short pilot using hosted credits, share Dedicated baseline for larger throughput needs, and schedule a technical deep dive for infra.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, I'm an AE here. with me is Priya Kapoor, our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:20] Dana: Dana Ortiz here, CTO at Silverpike. Mark Chen, ML eng. Asha Patel, security. Robert Ng from product.
[00:50] Jordan: Awesome, appreciate it. High-level goal for today's call is to understand your timeline and goals for a pilot, and figure out whether the hosted API credits get you to first call, or whether we should scope Dedicated or Private up front.
[01:30] Mark: Yeah we want TTFT in under a week ideally. We have a prototype using an open LLM but cost and latency are getting wild at scale.
[03:00] Priya (Redwood SE): Cool — can you give us a quick sense of your workload? token sizes, avg seq length, concurrency targets?
[03:20] Mark: Sure, average prompt is about 120 tokens, responses around 280 tokens. peak concurrency 40 RPS for a batch of users, but initial pilot is 5–10 RPS. a lot of prefix caching would help, we do a fair amount of re-use.
[04:10] Asha: security first — we need to know about data residency, retention, and KMS support. also SOC2, ISO, and audit logs.
[05:00] Jordan: Good call — we are SOC2 Type II, we provide audit logging for private and dedicated, hosted has retained logs for 30 days by default but can be configured. KMS integrations are available for Dedicated and Private (bring-your-own key), hosted supports customer-managed keys with enterprise plan. we'll share the security pack after the call (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack).
[06:10] Dana: If we start with hosted credits for TTFT, what are the realistic constraints? latency SLOs?
[07:00] Priya: For small pilots on hosted, median latency for a 400-token turn on our curated quantized models is usually 150–350ms depending on model choice and region, P95 might be higher — that's why we often recommend dedicated if you need predictable P95 at high throughput. Also streaming vs chunked responses impacts perceived latency.
[08:20] Mark: Curious about cost — Dedicated vs hosted unit economics?
[08:40] Jordan: Hosted is pay-as-you-go — simple pricing and credits can be used to offset early cost. Dedicated gives you lower per-token cost at committed throughput but requires a reserved contract. we can run a cost projection once we see your seq-length distribution. Priya will send a baseline spreadsheet.
[10:00] Priya: One thing to flag — model variants and quantization choices change both latency and output quality. For example, Q4_0 gives better quality than lower-bit quant but costs more. we'll suggest a couple of models tuned to your prefix reuse.
[12:00] Robert: How painful is migration from hosted to Dedicated or Private?
[12:30] Priya: It's intentionally designed to be seamless — same API surface, same routing, you can pin model versions and rollout policies. The main lift is network configuration (VPC peering, subnets) for Private. for Dedicated we handle autoscaling and capacity pools.
[14:10] Asha: On Private, do you support on-prem air-gapped installs? we have an enterprise line that may require that.
[14:40] Jordan: Yep — Private has an on-prem package for regulated workloads. leads to longer procurement cycle and extra support. we'll include that in the enterprise path doc.
[16:00] Mark: For the pilot, what's the minimal integration to get to first call?
[16:30] Priya: Typically: sign up, redeem credits, get API key, run a small conformance test (openapi/rv), and call the endpoint. we can provide a repo with sample code. TTFT can be < 24 hours for experienced teams, but conservatively plan 2–3 days including integration and simple evals.
[18:00] Dana: Security will need to review the SOC2 and KMS bit. Asha will own that. We also need SLA clarity for Dedicated.
[18:30] Asha: yes please send the SOC2 report summary and details on encryption at rest and in transit. also SSO/SAML for team access.
[19:20] Jordan: Noted. we'll attach SOC2 summary and SSO docs. (link: https://redwood.example.com/sso-guide)
[21:00] Robert: Any gotchas around request size or KV cache we should know?
[21:30] Priya: KV cache is a big win for steady-state latency — we can enable prefix caching on models that support it. request size limits exist per model, but we can suggest truncation strategies and early stopping. also batching can reduce cost but increases latency, so that's a tradeoff.
[23:10] Mark: For our early users we need < 500ms P95. can hosted hit that consistently?
[23:40] Priya: For low concurrency and the right model/region, yes. For sustained 40 RPS at tight P95, we'd recommend Dedicated and show you a baseline.
[25:00] Dana: timeline — we want to validate functionality in two weeks and decide whether to commit to Dedicated in 6–8 weeks. Is that realistic?
[25:40] Jordan: Yes — pilot on hosted for 1–2 weeks using credits, run perf checks; if you need Dedicated we'll scope capacity and proposals within that 6–8 week window.
[27:00] Asha: On data retention, can we disable logging for certain sensitive endpoints in hosted?
[27:30] Jordan: There are controls by route and token level in the Console; for anything sensitive we recommend Private or Dedicated with BYOK. we'll include a runbook excerpt.
[29:10] Mark: Could you run a quick spike: we can send a 1k sample queries and you'd run a smoke perf run on your hosted infra to see median/P95?
[29:35] Priya: Yep we can do that — please upload the sample queries to the secure S3 link we'll share. we'll run the smoke and return results in 48–72 hours.
[31:00] Jordan: I'll send the S3 upload instructions and the straightforward integration repo. linking the quickstart guide: https://redwood.example.com/quickstart and the credits redemption flow.
[33:00] Robert: One other question — third party compliance: we sometimes send data to an external vector DB; any concerns with that?
[33:30] Priya: As long as you control encryption and access, it's fine. for auditability use our tracing hooks and per-route logs. Dedicated/Private gives you stricter controls.
[35:00] Dana: OK let's recap next steps.
[35:15] Jordan: Recap: 1) Jordan sends pricing + credits instructions and S3 upload link. 2) Priya shares Dedicated perf baseline spreadsheet and will run a hosted smoke test on the provided sample queries. 3) Asha to review SOC2 and KMS notes and send any blocker questions. 4) Schedule a technical deep dive next week for infra folks.
[38:00] Asha: That works. Please include estimated cost band for Dedicated at 40 RPS in the baseline.
[38:30] Priya: Will do — I'll include a few capacity scenarios.
[40:00] Jordan: Great — thanks everybody. we'll follow up with the docs and meeting invites.
[41:30] Mark: thanks, bye.
[41:45] Dana: Bye.
